solution:
The classes are given in inclusive (discontinuous) form, so first convert them to continuous boundaries by subtracting \(0.5\) from each lower limit and adding \(0.5\) to each upper limit. Take \(A = 31\), \(h = 5\) and \(u_i = \dfrac{x_i - 31}{5}\).

| Given class | Boundaries | \(x_i\) | \(f_i\) | \(u_i\) | \(f_iu_i\) | \(f_iu_i^2\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 14-18 | 13.5-18.5 | 16 | 5 | \(-3\) | \(-15\) | 45 |
| 19-23 | 18.5-23.5 | 21 | 18 | \(-2\) | \(-36\) | 72 |
| 24-28 | 23.5-28.5 | 26 | 44 | \(-1\) | \(-44\) | 44 |
| 29-33 | 28.5-33.5 | 31 | 70 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 34-38 | 33.5-38.5 | 36 | 36 | 1 | 36 | 36 |
| 39-43 | 38.5-43.5 | 41 | 22 | 2 | 44 | 88 |
| 44-48 | 43.5-48.5 | 46 | 5 | 3 | 15 | 45 |
| Total | — | — | 200 | — | 0 | 330 |

(The correction leaves each midpoint unchanged but makes the width a true \(h = 5\).)

\(N = 200\), \(\Sigma f_iu_i = 0\), so \(\bar{x} = 31 + 5 \times \dfrac{0}{200} = 31\) cm.

\(\sigma^2 = h^2\left[\dfrac{\Sigma f_iu_i^2}{N} - \left(\dfrac{\Sigma f_iu_i}{N}\right)^2\right] = 25\left[\dfrac{330}{200} - 0\right] = 25 \times 1.65 = 41.25\).

\(\sigma = \sqrt{41.25} \approx 6.42\).

Variance \(= 41.25\); S.D. \(\approx 6.42\) cm

Let the other two observations be \(x\) and \(y\), with \(n = 5\), \(\bar{x} = 4.8\).

From the mean: \(\Sigma x_i = 5 \times 4.8 = 24\), and \(1+3+8 = 12\), so \(x + y = 24 - 12 = 12\).

From the variance: \(\dfrac{\Sigma x_i^2}{5} - (4.8)^2 = 6.56 \Rightarrow \dfrac{\Sigma x_i^2}{5} = 6.56 + 23.04 = 29.6\), so \(\Sigma x_i^2 = 148\).
Since \(1^2+3^2+8^2 = 74\), we get \(x^2 + y^2 = 148 - 74 = 74\).

Then \(2xy = (x+y)^2 - (x^2+y^2) = 144 - 74 = 70\), so \(xy = 35\).

Hence \(x\) and \(y\) are the roots of \(t^2 - 12t + 35 = 0\), i.e. \((t-5)(t-7) = 0\).

The other two observations are \(5\) and \(7\)
